title: Vocal Runway: request threads and patch-probe inventory
content:
Purpose: quick synthesis of a small-but-urgent cluster of customer feedback collected Aug 15–Aug 27 (support tickets, CS interviews, and field notes). Goal is to propose low-risk, quick probes (1–2 sprints) and surface any items that should be escalated to product/engineering.

Context and constraints:
- Customers: 6 mid-market and enterprise customers (financial, legal, ecommerce), mostly on Dedicated, 2 on Private.
- Common thread: unpredictable token-level latency spikes and occasional quality regressions after model rollouts or config changes (batching/kv-cache tuning). Many asks look like UX or routing polish, some are runtime patches.
- We prioritise low-risk experiments first: address top impact-with-low-effort items to buy time for larger engine work.

Raw notes (short extracts):
- "We saw a 3× spike on cold-start windows when sequence length > 2048 and many concurrent chat sessions. Sometimes responses hang for 6–12s" — Customer A (enterprise search).
- "After the last model swap we started seeing slightly worse follow-up answers on multi-turn flows; reverting to previous model fixed it" — Customer B (SaaS automation).
- "Embeddings throughput drops intermittently, looks like occasional scheduler thrashing when other teams hit long-gen jobs" — Customer C (recommendations).
- "We want a per-route override for prefix caching expiration, our prompts vary a lot across customers" — Customer D (legal).

Synthesis — themes and short hypotheses:
1) KV/prefix cache mismatch and eviction sensitivity
   - Hypothesis: common configurations cause suboptimal cache hit rates for mid-length convo workloads (~500–1500 tokens), creating extra KV rebuilds and transient latency spikes.
   - Evidence: telemetry spikes correlate with sessions where sequence length distributions are bimodal; customer requests for per-route cache TTLs.
2) Model variant fallback and rollout blindspots
   - Hypothesis: rollouts currently change hidden config knobs (kernel selection / quantization flags) and customers experience quality deltas; automated fallbacks are coarse.
   - Evidence: regression resolved on revert; notes in rollout logs show kernel selector heuristics changed on deployment.
3) Inter-tenant noisy neighbors on Dedicated pools
   - Hypothesis: multi-tenant scheduling or autoscaler reaction to long jobs causes throughput cliffs for embeddings/short responses.
   - Evidence: customers on same pool report intermittent mmidgen latency; infra logs show scheduler preemption events.

Proposed low-effort probes (ranked by impact/effort):
- Probe A: Per-route cache-ttl toggle (2–4 dev-days)
  - What: Add per-route override to prefix/KV cache TTL + opt-in flag in Console.
  - Why: Customers can reduce cache churn without requiring engine changes.
  - Success metric: reduce 95th-pct latency on affected customers by >25% within 2 weeks.
  - Risks: Slight memory uptick; need quota guardrails.

- Probe B: Canary knob to lock kernel-selection on rollout (3 dev-days)
  - What: Add a rollout flag to keep previous kernel/quant flags for a percentage of traffic during model swap.
  - Why: Allows safety net for quality regressions without full revert.
  - Success metric: lower rollback frequency; observed quality regression detection decreases.
  - Risks: Slight complexity to rollout flow; monitoring additions.

- Probe C: Dedicated pool scheduling soft-limits (5 dev-days + ops config)
  - What: Implement short soft-limits and backpressure for long-run jobs (e.g., capped concurrent long-gen slots) to avoid scheduler thrashing.
  - Why: Prevent noisy long jobs from destabilising short-gen throughput.
  - Success metric: embeddings throughput stable (p95) across pools under mixed workloads.
  - Risks: Could reduce max throughput for some customers; need clear docs and opt-in.

- Probe D: Embedding job tagging + prioritized queue (4 dev-days)
  - What: Allow customers to tag embedding requests (low/normal/high importance) so scheduler can prioritize critical requests.
  - Why: Quick way to surface customer intent to scheduler with low infra churn.
  - Success metric: reduced tail latency for tagged high-priority embedding jobs.
  - Risks: abuse; requires quota adjustments.

Quick impact x effort table (qualitative):
- Per-route cache-ttl toggle: High impact / Very low effort
- Kernel-lock rollout flag: Medium impact / Low effort
- Dedicated soft-limits: Medium-high impact / Medium effort
- Embedding tagging: Low-medium impact / Low effort

Telemetry asks (engineering):
- Add a KV-cache hit/miss heatmap per-tenant exposed in Console (minimum: 7-day window). Helps confirm hypothesis 1.
- Export per-model rollout kernel-select flags in rollout audit logs.
- Per-pool job-duration histogram to detect noisy neighbors.

Suggested owners & next steps:
- CS (Marisol + Ethan): validate these hypotheses with the 6 customers, collect short prompt/seq-length samples and traffic patterns (by Sep 6).
- Eng Runtime (owner suggestion: Priya): quick spike to prototype Probe A and Probe B (1 sprint each). Add telemetry hooks as part of these spikes.
- Platform/Ops (Luis): draft an opt-in schedule policy for Dedicated pools and test with Customer C in staging.

Open questions / unresolved:
- How much memory budget do we have per-customer for per-route TTLs? (who owns quotas)
- Will kernel-locking increase tail latency for some sequences? Need small A/B tests with synthetic workloads.
- Is there appetite to expose embedding priority to customers given potential for misuse? Need rate-limit guardrails.

Customer quotes to use when pushing for quick patches:
- "If we can avoid rollbacks and instead route 5% of our traffic to the old kernel while we validate, that would be huge." — Customer B
- "We don't need a full engine rewrite — a console knob for caching TTLs would buy us time and keep SLAs stable." — Customer D

Actionable checklist (first 14 days):
- [ ] CS: collect session traces from 6 customers and upload to shared folder (Marisol)
- [ ] Eng: add KV cache telemetry hooks to dev branch (Priya)
- [ ] Platform: prepare opt-in Dedicated pool policy doc and test plan (Luis)
- [ ] PM: schedule 30-min sync (CS/Runtime/Platform) week of Sep 7 to align on scope and owners (PM assigned: Tessa)

Appendix: quick reproducible test scaffold (notes for Eng)
- Synthetic workload: 60% short chats (<=300 tokens), 30% mid (500–1200), 10% long (>2000). Ramp concurrency to match Customer A peak patterns (120 concurrent sessions). Measure KV-cache miss rate and per-token latency over 30m windows. Use variant A: per-route TTL 60s; B: TTL 600s.

Slack/Link references:
- Thread: #cs-runtime (pinned message Aug 22) — contains raw transcripts.
- Linear: INF-842 (prefetch/kv tuning), INF-867 (rollout kernel audit)
- PR: runtime#364 (experimental kernel-locking implementation)

Notes to self: aim for low friction, measurable wins. If Probe A cuts p95 in half for even 1 major customer, promote to product backlog for a GA release in 6–8 weeks.
